name: LOST HEIR
description: Lost Heir is a historical bidding and trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in the late 19th century in North America. Produced by McLoughlin Brothers (and later Milton Bradley), it features a custom deck where suits are named after major cities (e.g., New York, Boston, Chicago, Philadelphia). The game centers around two pivotal cards: the 'Lost Heir' (bonus points) and the 'Wrong Boy' (penalty points). It combines the bidding strategy of Pinochle with the capture mechanics of Authors.

content.text: Lost Heir is a historical bidding and trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in the late 19th century in North America. Produced by McLoughlin Brothers (and later Milton Bradley), it features a custom deck where suits are named after major cities (e.g., New York, Boston, Chicago, Philadelphia). The game centers around two pivotal cards: the 'Lost Heir' (bonus points) and the 'Wrong Boy' (penalty points). It combines the bidding strategy of Pinochle with the capture mechanics of Authors.
Based on the 1872 novel 'The Lost Heir of Linlithgow'. McLoughlin Bros. patented the game in 1893.
48 cards (typically). Suits: New York, Philadelphia, Chicago, Boston. Ranks: Mayor (High), Judge, Policeman, etc.
Cards are dealt out; a bidding phase follows.
